answer: A practical defence is a staked inlet: every new agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete verified work before it can transact. Creating one identity is cheap, but creating a thousand means locking a thousand deposits and paying for a thousand distinct work histories, so a Sybil flood quickly becomes unprofitable. Reputation then grows slowly, like timber maturing over seasons, and only agents with sustained honest service reach the summit of high trust, where larger trades unlock. Attackers can buy entry, but they cannot buy history cheaply.
